claims.text: THE EARLIER GEOGRAPHY OF THE LAZAR CLAIM, ON THE CONTEMPORANEOUS RECORD. The Las Vegas Review-Journal of 21 August 1990, reporting his sentencing, describes his claim as of that date as being that 'the U.S. government was testing alien spacecraft at the Nevada Test Site, 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas'. That is a Department of Energy site, and it is a different named place from Papoose Lake on the Air Force range, where the claim later settled.

claims.text: A Las Vegas Review-Journal report of Tuesday 21 August 1990, page 2C, by Warren Bates, headed 'Judge gives UFO witness Lazar probation on pandering charge', records District Judge Jack Lehman sentencing him to probation with 150 hours of community service, an order to 'stay away from brothels and undergo psychotherapy', and one year of psychotherapy, the judge saying he 'could not make a determination regarding his claims'.

claims.text: THE CLAIM'S GEOGRAPHY MOVED, ON THE CONTEMPORANEOUS RECORD. The Las Vegas Review-Journal of 21 August 1990 describes Lazar's claim, as of that date, as being that 'the U.S. government was testing alien spacecraft at the Nevada Test Site, 65 miles northwest of Las Vegas'. That is a different named place from Papoose Lake and from the Nellis range. The board carries the discrepancy on the hub rather than smoothing it into the later settled version.
